title: How Content Packaging and Pattern Interrupts Drive Social Media Views
summary: The creator explains how pattern interrupts and creative packaging captivate audiences and dramatically increase view counts. By incorporating unique personal traits into content presentation, creators can trigger dopamine responses that keep viewers engaged. To convert views into actual business leads, content must balance unique packaging with clear value relevant to the offer.
key_points: Interrupting standard patterns (such as painting synchronously to music) triggers a dopamine response that encourages viewers to keep watching.
Proper content packaging can increase view counts from thousands to tens of millions (e.g., artist Matt Chessco reached 11.4M, 17.3M, and 26.4M views).
Successful creators and businesses prioritize how they present and package their offers rather than solely focusing on what they are selling.
Standout packaging does not require high-end editing or elaborate costumes.

Package work by leveraging unique personal traits or hobbies outside of your main industry (e.g., a financial advisor creating songs about investments or a movie-obsessed chef making cinematic cooking videos).
To generate actual business leads rather than just views, ensure the content delivers real value tied directly to your niche and offer.
content:
Post Text:
This artist got 26.4 MILLION views – and although the art is amazing, the video went viral because of something tied to our human psychology.

And we see this across industries. 

(Another amazing example of this is @tigrangertz and his landscaping team doing silly videos and skits to set themselves apart from other landscaping companies!)

And it doesn’t mean you have to over-perform to sell your product/service/art – it just means that HOW you present your content can influence how your audience engages with it.

Here’s how you can use this concept in your content:

You can get super creative and come up with something fun like these guys, but you don’t have to wrack your brain for an idea.

Instead, I recommend finding something about you and your life outside of your work that you can package your product or service in to give you an edge.

Maybe you’re a financial advisor who is also a musician, so you create songs about different investments.

Maybe you’re a private chef that’s obsessed with movies, so you create cooking videos in the style of your favorite films.

Maybe you’re a dietitian that’s really sarcastic, so you explain various concepts as if you’re talking to your annoying 12 year old brother.

Whatever it is, there’s something unique about you that can be spun creatively to make some awesome content!

One important thing to remember, however, is that this type of content is great for getting views, but if you want to get leads or business from social media, make sure your content has value that ties back to your niche and what you’re selling so people can actually be motivated to buy from you.

Creator featured: @mattchessco

Make a note of this post.

Spoken Audio Transcript:
This creator proves that packaging sells. He could have just slowly revealed his art like everybody else and gotten several thousand views. But instead, he got 11 million, 17 million, 26 million views, all thanks to something backed by human psychology. Our brains look for patterns. So the moment that pattern is interrupted by a unique approach, like painting to music, that interruption triggers a dopamine response, and now we want to keep watching. And you see it across industries, the businesses that get the most attention don't focus on what they are selling. They focus on how they package what they're selling to make it stand out in the market. And any creator can do this, but you don't have to have insane editing or dress like Avatar. I'll put some examples in the caption.
